The source directly states that under 300,000 sessions per month in 2025, brands are far better taking much bigger swings.
The alternative-to relation with comprehensive CRO is consistent with the source's two-bucket session-based framing.
The noted count inconsistency between 'six to eight' and 'eight' is a real ambiguity acknowledged in the candidate.
The source states that over 300,000 sessions per month, with good enough conversion rate and enough orders, there is enough data for comprehensive full CRO.
The action description matches the source's list of AB testing, data analysis, long audits, and deep data work.
The alternative-to relation with the under-300,000-session approach is supported by the source's two-bucket framing.
The source explicitly says driving media straight to PDPs, product pages, homepages, or collection pages leaves money on the table.
The action to insert a landing page between post-click and store landing is directly stated and explained as pre-selling before money pages.
The source warns that not using LPS, listicles, sales pages, advertorials, or different angles leaves money on the table.
The action to test listicles and advertorials is directly stated by the source.
The source states that under 300,000 sessions, testing button color, an above-fold image, or small text snippets is no longer the approach.

The source lists isolated AB tests with incremental increases in revenue per visitor as part of comprehensive CRO.

source_limitations: The excerpt is a transcript containing speech-to-text errors and ambiguous phrases such as 'advvertorial', 'listical', 'G4', 'iOS 4 tracking 14 tracking', and 'three for the power of two', so some quoted terms may be transcription artifacts.
The excerpt begins mid-discussion and ends mid-sentence, so surrounding context, later promised explanations, case studies, and examples referenced by the speaker are not available for review.
The source provides no independent data, methodology, sample sizes, time periods, statistical thresholds, or platform documentation for the numerical examples and performance claims.
The 300,000 sessions per month threshold is described as an internal benchmark that changed in the last six to twelve months, not an externally validated cutoff.
The excerpt does not define 'good enough' conversion rate, 'enough orders', 'enough data', the two solutions, or behavior exactly at 300,000 sessions.
The source includes personal opinion and promotional/sponsorship content, which cannot be independently verified from this excerpt alone.
